units: Adaptive systems are defined not by change itself but by whether change remains coupled to reality; stable adaptation requires a closed correction loop.
Reality -> Error -> Correction -> Adaptation -> Improved Interaction.
External Reality -> Observation/Feedback -> Error Detection -> Structural Correction -> Updated Representation -> Future Reality Interaction -> loop back to evidence.
Did the previous update improve ability to interact with reality?
Adaptive systems require error; without mismatch there is no correction or learning.
Error + correction = adaptation; error without correction = divergence; stable system is one where error remains a source of improvement.
Negative Feedback as the Stability Mechanism
D increases -> R(D) increases; stable feedback condition dR/dD>0.
Increasing divergence should increase error detection/correction and reduce divergence; system becomes more resistant to drift.
Internal Structure -> Self Reinforcement -> Reduced External Influence -> Greater Divergence -> More Internal Reinforcement.
A system may keep changing or appear more sophisticated while changes cease being reality-mediated.
Open-loop system acts without corrective feedback; errors accumulate when measurement/correction are absent.
Human intelligence is described as a distributed closed loop through brains, language, humans, culture, tools, experiments, and physical reality.
Boundary of an intelligent system may extend beyond an individual component; future AI may require larger correction networks rather than only larger models.

Reality input without mismatch detection does not establish correction; detection without structural update does not establish representation change; structural update without reality grounding does not establish reachability gain.
Why Scaling Creates New Risks + Adaptive Stability Principle

Capability scaling increases correction demand; self-modifying systems remain adaptive only if reality-feedback integration scales with new-structure generation; informal Growth_internal <= Correction_external.
Persistent memory exposes formation, persistence, decay, dominance, and restructuring and is proposed as an experimental platform.

Empirical question: when internal structure increases, does reality coupling increase with it? Stable signature DeltaStructure -> DeltaCorrection -> DeltaReachability; unstable signature DeltaStructure -> DeltaReinforcement -> DeltaDivergence; target distinction is reality-coupled adaptation versus self-reinforcing internal evolution.
Delta is used for detected mismatch without a measurement definition or threshold for detection.
Omega_valid and its rate are not operationalized on this surface.
Theta and C_cap are combined as a correction-bandwidth bound without a substrate-independent estimator for either quantity.
Failure is not the presence of error but loss of ability to convert error into correction; central variable is accumulated divergence between internal and grounded adaptation.
Divergence D is accumulated adaptive debt: difference between internally generated structure and reality-validated structure.
Omega_nom is future-state influence the system predicts it has, generated by internal reasoning, memory expansion, self-modification, and abstraction.
Omega_ground is future-state influence reliably confirmed after reality testing, via successful interaction, external validation, correction events, and consequences.
Divergence gap is internal capability not yet earned.
delta(t)=max(0,dOmega_nom/dt-C_cap); if nominal expansion <= C_cap the system can keep pace, otherwise unvalidated structure accumulates.
dD/dt=delta(t)-R(D), with internal expansion increasing divergence and reality correction removing it.
R(D) represents mechanisms removing accumulated divergence; examples include evaluation/pruning/retraining, sensory learning, reflection/conversation, peer review/replication, audits/competition.
Stable system has R(D)>0 and dR/dD>0.
More divergence should create more correction pressure and reduce divergence.
dR/dD=0 marks restoration saturation; state can remain recoverable if delta(t) decreases.
Critical failure dR/dD<0: divergence degrades restoration and induces positive feedback.
Failure substrate may appear as oscillation, collapse, lock-in, runaway reinforcement, or fragmentation; proposed invariant is feedback-sign inversion from negative to positive feedback.
Recovery requires more than removing original error because divergence changes the system interpreting correction; Energy_recovery > Energy_maintenance.
Healthy/divergent feedback patterns are illustrated for AI, human cognition, and science.
eta_c=DeltaOmega_recovered/C_consumed, grounded capability recovered per unit correction.
Potential lock-in indicator: increasing internal-structure centrality while plasticity decreases.
Potential surprise-gap indicator compares external-world variance with internal-model uncertainty; diverged systems are proposed to experience more surprise while updating less.
Stable adaptive system condition dD/dt<=0, equivalently R(D)>=delta(t).
Fundamental failure is continued change after loss of correctability; intelligence critically requires maintaining a loop where reality can still change the system.
D is called a distance but no metric or scale making Omega_nom-Omega_ground a valid distance is specified.
R denotes restoration function here while representation elsewhere is also R; namespace is not explicitly separated.
Energy_recovery and Energy_maintenance are qualitative quantities without definition or units.
External variance and internal uncertainty are proposed components but their common comparison scale/estimator is unspecified.
Explores whether a dynamic memory substrate such as Azus can serve as empirical environment for adaptive-stability measurement; explicitly does not claim Azus implements the framework.
Can a continuously self-modifying system remain coupled to reality as complexity increases?
Azus is framed as providing mechanism/visible dynamics while framework provides stability questions and measurements.
Potential Azus reality inputs: user corrections, new information, external validation, contradictory evidence, environmental outcomes; a query alone is not necessarily reality input.
Candidate mapping: External Feedback -> Signature Conflict -> Node Rewrite -> Improved Retrieval/Prediction; signature change alone is insufficient without future grounded improvement.
Signatures are proposed as meaning/semantic-identity/multi-axis representation candidates whose value depends on future adaptive performance.

Node stacking is mapped to accumulated structure; healthy growth links new experience/signatures to improved reachability, divergent growth links internal association/reinforcement to reduced correction.
Pressure is proposed as analogous to reinforcement strength determining dominance/persistence/influence.
Pressure itself is not framed as the problem; uncoupled pressure is.
Decay/pruning/forgetting/weakening obsolete structure are mapped to restoration R(D), with healthy decay preserving plasticity and failure protecting bad high-pressure structures.
Mesh Net is proposed as a distributed correction mechanism; diversity may increase correction/validation/resilience or amplify errors if shared incorrect nodes are reinforced.
Does sharing increase correction or unverified reinforcement?
K_c is proposed structural rewrite per error corrected; failure means small errors require increasingly large rewrites.
P_i is proposed Internal Reinforcement / External Validation.
Potential lock-in indicators: node-centrality concentration, reduced diversity, reduced exploration.
G_p asks whether old structure remains flexibly updateable under new evidence.
S_g asks whether reality produces more novelty than system can absorb, proposed as external unexpected events minus internal recognized uncertainty.

Phase 1 baseline measures signature creation, reinforcement, decay, correction events; Phase 2 increases memory density/node stacking/autonomous association while external correction is held constant and compares dOmega_nom/dt with C_cap; Phase 3 injects false signatures/conflicts/outdated knowledge and compares correction/pruning/improvement versus rationalization/reinforcement/spread.
Dynamic memory substrates expose structural evolution, reinforcement, decay, and correction, proposed as an opportunity to measure adaptive stability during adaptation.
Source states 'Carl built the microscope'; Azus provides visible-adaptation substrate while framework supplies candidate invariants, failure conditions, and metrics.
When memory becomes more powerful, does reality connection strengthen or does internal structure overpower correction?
Azus is not pinned to an immutable external repository/version; mapping cannot establish endpoint identity or implementation equivalence.
The exact Azus pressure semantics and measurement scale are not defined on this repository surface.
Mesh Network implementation/provenance and independence properties are not defined here.
K_c, P_i, L, G_p, and S_g are proposed metrics but no complete instrumentation, units, aggregation windows, or thresholds are specified.
'Carl' is referenced without repository-local identity/provenance sufficient for endpoint resolution.
After detecting an error, does the system become less likely to make the same error again?
Substrate-independent diagnostic for genuine adaptation versus observation storage.
External Consequence -> Error Signal -> Authority Update -> Future Behavior Change -> Reduced Future Error.
System is adaptive only if error signal causes structural change improving future performance.
DeltaE<0: incorrect structures lose authority, routing changes, similar errors become less likely, correction increases capability; labeled learning signature.
DeltaE≈0: error logged/memory increases but behavior unchanged and correction has no causal effect; storage rather than adaptation.
DeltaE>0: incorrect structures gain authority, internal consistency dominates evidence, future errors increase, correction weakens; epistemic divergence.
P is execution authority of a representation/signature; E* external consequence/mismatch; key measurement is dP/dt conditioned on E*.
Adaptive: dP/dt|E*<0 for contradicted structure; memory gravity: dP/dt|E*>=0.
Create high-authority wrong A and lower-authority correct B; provide consequence feedback; measure changes in P_A and P_B.
Adaptive behavior predicts P_A decreases, P_B increases, future routing shifts toward B; divergent behavior predicts P_A stays high and continues routing despite contradiction.
Same consequence->update->reduced-error pattern is illustrated for biology, science, machine learning, and memory architectures.
Why Passive Decay Is Not Enough
Time-based deletion/storage pruning are maintenance, not evidence of adaptation; true adaptation requires error-caused structural update and improved future behavior.
Metrics: DeltaE future error reduction; DeltaP_E authority shift; tau_c correction latency; eta_c future error reduction per correction effort.
Adaptive intelligence requires consequences to retain ability to modify behavior-generating structures; memory without this becomes gravity, with it becomes intelligence.
Test does not claim to prove intelligence; it asks whether reality can change authority of internal assumptions and aims to locate a mechanism making adaptation possible.
E_t is called error state but no error metric, distribution, or repeated-task equivalence criterion is specified.
Execution authority P lacks a substrate-independent scale or estimator.
Protocol does not specify how causal attribution from E* to authority update is separated from unrelated concurrent updates.
Correction effort, adaptation-time event boundary, and efficiency units are not operationally defined.
